topic: K1 Define a triangular class for scalar bounded causal features and K<K_n with unique interior quantizers, controlled curvature and margin, nuisance rate r_n, adjacent score variance sigma_{P,K}^2=Var(phi_{rho,K+1}-phi_{rho,K}), and minimum standardized gap min_K [rho(K+1)-rho(K)]/sigma_{P,K}. K2 derive the maximal joint growth region for K_n, standardized gap, curvature, margin, and r_n that permits simultaneous bands and locally honest set-valued profiles, plus the complementary failure boundary. K3 construct a corrected-moment growing-class bootstrap attaining it. K4 prove a matching adjacent-quantization lower bound. Use U uniform on [0,1] and MineThatData as witness and consumer.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp joint growth region in K_n, minimum adjacent standardized gap, K-dependent curvature and margin constants, and causal nuisance rate r_n under which corrected estimates of the full scalar causal-quantization resolution profile admit a simultaneous multiplier-bootstrap band?

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature supplies three separate pieces—fixed-K causal orthogonality, K-sensitive quantizer geometry, and high-dimensional multiplier bands—but no theorem composes them when Voronoi cells, curvature, adjacent variances, and nuisance tolerances all deteriorate with K. The prior functional-DiD proposal independently leaves necessity of an orthogonal causal band condition open and its reviewer demands a genuine undercoverage packing. Here the first missing step is a K-uniform Bahadur expansion for optimized causal distortion, with codebook reoptimization and nuisance remainder measured coordinatewise against sigma_{P,K}; the failure side must exhibit actual undercoverage rather than merely violate sufficient assumptions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient up-to-logarithms system of explicit inequalities in K_n, the minimum standardized adjacent gap, curvature and margin sequences, and r_n, plus a corrected-score multiplier bootstrap with uniform vanishing coverage error and a complementary triangular-array undercoverage construction.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from population summaries to interpretable causal subgroup structure is the closest framing; the new destination is honest inference over the resolution index.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Population causal summaries hide heterogeneous structure -> causal k-means makes subgroup resolution a target -> analysts inspect several K values -> growing-resolution inference needs one jointly honest profile band

method_exemplars.technique: Prove a uniform orthogonal-score Bahadur representation, apply a high-dimensional Gaussian approximation, and bootstrap estimated scores; replace fixed score regularity by K-dependent codebook and variance bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired object is a growing vector of orthogonal causal functionals, except that each coordinate here is an optimized nonsmooth quantization risk.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its margin-to-quadratic-growth inequality and localized empirical-process argument while retaining cell-mass, separation, and margin-radius dependence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those geometric constants are precisely the quantities that must control the reoptimization remainder in the joint growth region.

method_exemplars.technique: Use hyperrectangle Gaussian approximation, multiplier comparison, covariance-discrepancy bounds, and Gaussian anti-concentration after coordinatewise studentization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The band statistic is the maximum of a growing correlated vector of standardized adjacent causal scores.

open_problems.open_problem: For U uniform on [0,1], what is the exact finite-K variance and cross-K covariance kernel of the full adjacent efficient scores phi_{rho,K+1}-phi_{rho,K}, and which growing-K studentization regime remains valid as those variances vanish?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact integration verifies W(K)=1/(12K^2) and Var(loss_K)=1/(180K^4). It also shows, for the known-feature raw losses, Cov(loss_K,loss_{K+1})=1/[180K^4(K+1)^4], so cancellation does not change the K^-4 order and the normalized known-scale adjacent score has standardized gap asymptotic to sqrt(5/2)/K. The unresolved object is the full causal efficient score, including scale-functional, nuisance, and cross-fitted correction terms, and its covariance for nonadjacent K and L. Those terms determine the standardized envelope and covariance estimation error needed by a growing-dimensional bootstrap, while the available Gaussian approximation assumes its nondegeneracy conditions rather than deriving them for this array.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A closed-form formula and uniform asymptotic equivalent for sigma_{P,K}^2 and Cov(phi_{rho,K+1}-phi_{rho,K}, phi_{rho,L+1}-phi_{rho,L}) under U[0,1], followed by a studentized Gaussian or multiplier-bootstrap theorem with explicit maximal K_n and a counterexample at the first failed standardized-envelope condition.

writing_exemplar.why: Its efficient-score causal-clustering setup makes the hidden adjacent-resolution variance the natural next inferential object.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal k-means yields efficient fixed-resolution scores -> choosing resolution compares adjacent risks -> raw gaps are meaningless without adjacent-score noise -> exact studentized-gap geometry determines feasible growing-K inference

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate the quantization objective at its unique optimum and use centroid first-order conditions to remove first-order codebook perturbations before forming adjacent covariances.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired score is the optimized-distortion derivative, and Pollard's center CLT supplies the relevant envelope-theorem and Hessian move.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply rectangle Gaussian comparison and multiplier coupling after coordinatewise variance normalization, using the computed standardized envelope in place of the generic envelope sequence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once adjacent variances and covariances are explicit, the profile statistic is a maximum of a growing standardized score vector.

open_problems.open_problem: Under K-dependent uniqueness, curvature, cell-mass, and margin sequences, how uniformly stable is the estimated scalar causal-feature codebook over every K<=K_n, and exactly when is its optimized-risk contribution second order relative to the adjacent-score scale?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fixed-k consistency suppresses the deterioration that controls this problem: in scalar high-rate quantization, cell probability and center separation are order 1/K, while the objective Hessian, boundary margin tube, and estimated causal feature also change with K. The first proof step that fails is the fixed-K margin-to-quadratic-growth argument: its constants must be uniformized and combined with a cross-fitted perturbation bound. Until then, the heuristic codebook excess risk near 1/(nK) cannot be rigorously compared with sigma_{P,K}/sqrt(n), and it is unknown whether codebook error or causal nuisance error reaches first order first.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform-in-K high-probability matched-codebook and excess-causal-distortion bound with explicit curvature, margin, separation, and cell-mass dependence, plus an if-and-only-if characterization of when the reoptimization remainder is o_P(sigma_{P,K}/sqrt(n)) for all K<=K_n.

writing_exemplar.why: Its route from geometric regularity constants to codebook error and sharp risk is the closest framing, with K dependence and causal nuisance perturbation becoming the destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fast quantization needs local geometric regularity -> margin and separation turn risk into codebook distance -> growing K deteriorates those constants -> causal-feature codebooks need a uniform stability and remainder frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Port the margin-based quadratic-growth lemma and localized Gaussian-complexity fixed-point bound while keeping all dependence on minimum cell mass, center separation, margin radius, and K.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested object is a K-explicit version of its codebook-distance and excess-risk machinery.

method_exemplars.technique: Cross-fit the causal-feature nuisance and use Neyman orthogonality to reduce first-order nuisance bias to a product-rate remainder, then compare it uniformly with the shrinking score scale.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The codebook is fit to an unknown causal feature, so its stability proof must incorporate the same orthogonal cross-fitting mechanism that permits flexible nuisance estimation.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Near a tie between K and K+1, selecting one resolution is nonregular: the same standardized gaps determine both coverage and the cardinality of an honest report. Published moment-selection theory starts from supplied moments, but these inequalities are differences of optimized causal risks sharing nuisance estimates and moving codebooks. The prior tail-index proposal supplies a finite-grid honest-set and matching-contiguity blueprint, yet its three-valued tail experiment does not transfer: the first new step is a joint covariance-normalized local experiment for several adjacent optimized distortions, whose ambiguity geometry is a correlated chain of inequalities.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A simultaneous score-inversion set of admissible resolutions with uniform coverage of the population near-optimal set, together with a local Gaussian-experiment theorem and matching Le Cam ambiguity bound characterizing when the report is singleton versus must contain adjacent K values as gaps cross the √(log K_n/n) scale.

writing_exemplar.why: Its causal subgroup-resolution narrative reaches the destination directly; the new issue is honest reporting when neighboring resolutions are observationally tied.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal k-means makes heterogeneity resolution interpretable -> neighboring resolutions can have nearly equal gains -> selecting one K becomes nonregular -> honest analysis must report a set of admissible resolutions

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt generalized moment selection and its uniform local-size proof, treating each adjacent gain as an inequality after establishing corrected quantization-score regularity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The profile is a confidence set determined by which adjacent inequalities are binding, the same nonregular geometry handled by generalized moment selection.

method_exemplars.technique: Use studentized max-bootstrap critical values and discard clearly slack coordinates while preserving potentially binding ones, with a uniform proof for the selection event.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The K_n adjacent comparisons form a growing correlated moment-inequality system.

method_exemplars.why_closest: Unavoidable profile ambiguity is the discrete-set analogue of the unavoidable length of an honest adaptive confidence interval.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Classical lower bounds target fixed-k excess distortion and may use globally difficult source distributions. This frontier instead requires contiguous causal laws that preserve boundedness, uniqueness, interiority, K-dependent curvature and margin, a uniform marginal witness, and prescribed nuisance difficulty while changing an adjacent gain. The prior CATE-level-set proposal identifies the analogous obstruction: a natural fuzzy family incurs excessive transition-region divergence under a uniform full-support design. The first missing step is therefore a mass-preserving perturbation—such as paired conditional-mark transports—aligned with the adjacent efficient score, followed by exact optimizer-stability and likelihood-distance checks.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A certified two-point or Assouad family inside the triangular causal-quantizer class and a Le Cam or Fano lower bound showing that uniform profile recovery or coverage fails whenever the standardized gap, K_n, curvature or margin, or r_n violates the upper frontier, matching the attainable region up to logarithms.

writing_exemplar.why: It keeps the scientific target as interpretable causal heterogeneity resolution and makes an impossibility boundary the natural limit on how fine that resolution can honestly be.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal clustering makes heterogeneity resolution estimable -> finer K reveals more structure but shrinks adjacent gains -> nuisance and codebook noise eventually erase distinctions -> a matching lower bound defines the honest resolution limit

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its separated quantization distributions and Assouad minimax comparison while enforcing prescribed margin, separation, and cell-mass sequences.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves the nearest sharp quantization lower bound; the new family must localize that machinery to adjacent K gains and a causal observed-data law.

method_exemplars.technique: Use localized outcome-regression and propensity perturbations to embed source-feature separation while maintaining nuisance constraints and controlling observed-law divergence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The lower bound must perturb an identified causal feature through observed data rather than assume that the feature is directly observed.

method_exemplars.technique: Use bounded-support packing distributions to force distortion redundancy, then change the testing loss to failure of adjacent-profile recovery.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its lower-bound object is empirical quantizer distortion on bounded support, the closest classical analogue to adjacent-quantization impossibility.

literature_map:
1. Kim, Kim & Kennedy (2026, JRSSB; arXiv:2405.03083) is the direct anchor: causal k-means, margin-controlled plug-in rates, and efficient bias-corrected root-n inference for a chosen clustering target.
2. Its discussion leaves problem-specific efficiency analysis for generic pseudo-outcomes but does not supply growing-K profile inference.
3. Pollard (1982, Annals of Probability; DOI 10.1214/AOP/1176993713) gives fixed-k center CLTs under uniqueness, density regularity, and positive curvature.
4. Pollard (1982, IEEE TIT; DOI 10.1109/TIT.1982.1056481) transfers fixed-k asymptotics to vector quantization, not adjacent-K triangular arrays.
5. Levrard (2013, Electronic Journal of Statistics; arXiv:1201.6052) proves O(1/n) fixed-level empirical-quantization risk under regularity.
6. Levrard (2015, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1405.6672) exposes margin radius, cell mass, separation, and quadratic-growth constants and proves a minimax lower bound, but not a K_n-growing theory.
7. Liu & Pagès (2020, JMLR 21) study convergence of optimal quantizers with K-dependent constants rather than a sharp simultaneous growth frontier.
8. Bartlett, Linder & Lugosi (1997, EuroCOLT; DOI 10.1007/3-540-62685-9_18) give a bounded-support quantizer-design lower bound for global distortion redundancy, not adjacent-K testing.
9. Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Econometrics Journal; arXiv:1608.00060) supply orthogonal moments and cross-fitting for causal targets with flexible nuisance estimates.
10. Belloni et al. (2018, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1512.07619) extend orthogonal-score inference to many functional targets and bootstrap estimated scores.
11. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov & Kato (2017, Annals of Probability; DOI 10.1214/16-AOP1113) establish high-dimensional Gaussian and bootstrap approximation for hyperrectangles under coordinate nondegeneracy.
12. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov & Koike (2021; arXiv:2012.09513) sharpen approximation rates for nondegenerate covariance but do not derive conditions for optimized scores with shrinking raw variances.
13. Andrews & Soares (2010, Econometrica) and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov & Kato (2019, ReStud; arXiv:1312.7614) provide locally uniform inference for binding and slack inequalities, not adjacent causal-quantization gains with moving codebooks.
14. The unoccupied intersection is fixed-K causal semiparametrics plus K-explicit quantization geometry plus growing-dimensional bootstrap, with the standardized adjacent-gap frontier, locally honest profile, and matching converse absent from the targeted scan.
